summary: Market sentiment is broadly risk-off, with Wall Street's fear gauge — the VIX — surging and traders positioning for further volatility, reflecting a cautious mood heading into a busy earnings week. Geopolitical tensions are a significant macro driver, with ongoing conflict in Yemen involving Houthi missile strikes near Saudi infrastructure, West Bank unrest, and Middle East instability pressuring energy markets, while the U.S. soliciting up to 17 million barrels from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve signals concern about supply dynamics. At the stock level, CoreWeave suffered a sharp selloff tied to stress in the debt market, dragging sentiment across AI-linked names including implications for OpenAI and Anthropic valuations, while Kimberly-Clark bucked the trend with its best weekly performance in four years on solid fundamentals, and a retail name was downgraded by analysts after its recent rally. Key risks investors are monitoring include AI sector fragility amid rising financing costs, geopolitical escalation in the Middle East disrupting energy supply chains, and growing concerns around AI espionage flagged by former SEC Chair Jay Clayton. In the short term, markets will look to Capital One and Meta earnings next week for directional clarity, but with the VIX elevated and geopolitical and credit market pressures mounting, the bias remains cautiously negative heading into the weekend.
